\section{Experimental Results}

\subsection{Setup}
We evaluate on \textbf{20 Craft tasks} with \textbf{10 test seeds} each (200 seed--task trials per run).
A task counts as \emph{solved} if at least one seed succeeds.
Baselines synthesize Python functions directly (no DSL); the pipeline synthesizes programs in an evolved DSL.
Five independent pipeline runs and five independent baseline runs, HuggingFace LLM, June~11, 2026.
We report \textbf{mean $\pm$ range} across completed runs (not best-of-$n$), because run-to-run variance is large.
Single-run highs are noted separately as highlighted results.

\subsection{Aggregate Comparison}

\begin{table}[htbp]
\centering
\caption{Aggregate comparison across independent runs (mean $\pm$ range). Baseline: $n{=}4$ (Run~5 incomplete). Pipeline DSL~0: $n{=}5$. Pipeline DSL~1: $n{=}3$ (Runs~3--5 only; Runs~1--2 did not reach DSL~1 evaluation at report time).}
\label{tab:aggregate-comparison}
\begin{tabular}{lccc}
\toprule
Metric & Baseline & Pipeline DSL~0 & Pipeline DSL~1 \\
\midrule
Tasks solved  & $13.5$ {\small [13--15]}  & $7.8$ {\small [3--19]}   & $12.7$ {\small [2--18]} \\
Seeds solved  & $129.8$ {\small [119--146]} & $51.2$ {\small [11--170]} & $101.7$ {\small [2--152]} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

On \emph{typical} behavior, mean baseline performance exceeds mean pipeline DSL~0 on both tasks and seeds.
Mean pipeline DSL~1 closes much of the task gap ($12.7$ vs.\ $13.5$) but remains below baseline on seeds ($101.7$ vs.\ $129.8$).
\textbf{Highlighted best runs} (not used for the headline comparison): Baseline Run~1 ($15/20$, $146/200$); pipeline Run~2 DSL~0 ($19/20$, $170/200$), which exceeds the best baseline on both metrics; pipeline Runs~3--4 DSL~1 ($18/20$ tasks each).

\subsection{DSL Evolution Gains (Runs with DSL~1)}

Runs~1 and~2 did not reach DSL~1 evaluation; Runs~3, 4, and~5 did.
Table~\ref{tab:dsl-evolution-gains} quantifies the DSL~0 $\rightarrow$ DSL~1 change for each.

\begin{table}[htbp]
\centering
\caption{DSL~0 $\rightarrow$ DSL~1 change for all runs with DSL~1 data (Runs~3--5). $\Delta$ = DSL~1 $-$ DSL~0.}
\label{tab:dsl-evolution-gains}
\resizebox{\textwidth}{!}{%
\begin{tabular}{lccccccccc}
\toprule
& \multicolumn{3}{c}{Run~3} & \multicolumn{3}{c}{Run~4} & \multicolumn{3}{c}{Run~5} \\
\cmidrule(lr){2-4} \cmidrule(lr){5-7} \cmidrule(lr){8-10}
Metric & DSL~0 & DSL~1 & $\Delta$ & DSL~0 & DSL~1 & $\Delta$ & DSL~0 & DSL~1 & $\Delta$ \\
\midrule
Tasks solved & 4/19  & 18/20 & +14 & 3/20  & 18/20 & +15 & 3/20  & 2/20  & $-$1 \\
Seeds solved & 10/190 & 151/200 & +141 & 30/200 & 152/199 & +122 & 11/200 & 2/200 & $-$9 \\
Rel.\ tasks   & \multicolumn{3}{c}{$\approx$4.5$\times$} & \multicolumn{3}{c}{6$\times$} & \multicolumn{3}{c}{0.67$\times$} \\
Rel.\ seeds   & \multicolumn{3}{c}{$\approx$15$\times$} & \multicolumn{3}{c}{$\approx$5$\times$} & \multicolumn{3}{c}{0.18$\times$} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}}
\end{table}

\begin{table}[htbp]
\centering
\caption{Side-by-side DSL~0 vs.\ DSL~1 summary for Runs~3--5 (rows: DSL round; columns: pipeline run).}
\label{tab:dsl0-vs-dsl1-all}
\begin{tabular}{lcccccc}
\toprule
& \multicolumn{2}{c}{Run~3} & \multicolumn{2}{c}{Run~4} & \multicolumn{2}{c}{Run~5} \\
\cmidrule(lr){2-3} \cmidrule(lr){4-5} \cmidrule(lr){6-7}
DSL Round & Tasks & Seeds & Tasks & Seeds & Tasks & Seeds \\
\midrule
DSL~0 & 4/19  & 10/190  & 3/20  & 30/200  & 3/20  & 11/200 \\
DSL~1 & 18/20 & 151/200 & 18/20 & 152/199 & 2/20  & 2/200 \\
\midrule
$\Delta$ & +14 & +141 & +15 & +122 & $-$1 & $-$9 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\textbf{Run~3} improves by +14 tasks and +141 seeds with no per-task regressions; most crafting tasks jump from 0/10 on DSL~0 to 10/10 on DSL~1.
\textbf{Run~4} improves by +15 tasks and +122 seeds, reaching a similar DSL~1 level as Run~3; the only regression is \texttt{get\_iron} (10/10 $\rightarrow$ 8/10).
\textbf{Run~5} regresses on DSL~1 ($-$1 task, $-$9 seeds): gathering tasks \texttt{get\_grass}, \texttt{get\_iron}, and \texttt{get\_wood} lose seeds, and DSL~1 never exceeds the weak DSL~0 baseline for this run.
Overall, DSL evolution is highly beneficial when DSL~0 performs poorly (Runs~3--4), but not guaranteed to help when the run is already unstable (Run~5).

\subsection{Hard Tasks}
\texttt{make\_clothbundleextra} was never solved in any completed run.
\texttt{make\_goldhammer} reached at most 3/10 seeds in the pipeline and 0/10 in all baselines.
